what_was_tried: 1. Installed docker.io on test VM (ubuntu@192.168.1.41) via apt-get install -y docker.io.
2. scp'd images/workspace-default/Dockerfile to ~/palmux-image-build/workspace-default/Dockerfile on the VM.
3. Started `cd ~/palmux-image-build/workspace-default && sudo docker build -t palmux-workspace:local .` over ssh, with output captured via `tail -100`.

4. After ~20 minutes the build was still running (`ps -p <pid>` showed an alive ssh process whose elapsed time was climbing) but the VM stopped accepting new SSH connections — every attempt got 'Connection timed out during banner exchange' on port 22.

5. Killed the build's wrapping ssh from our side; the VM did NOT recover. Multiple ssh probes over the next ~10 minutes all timed out at banner exchange. ICMP (ping) still works, port 22 still accepts TCP connections, but sshd does not send a banner — consistent with sshd or its accept loop being starved by the docker build's resource use.
what_was_completed_anyway: tests/acceptance/s0f6866_image.py:TestImageBuild.test_image_size_under_1gb covers AC-1-1 — once the VM recovers, running this test on it confirms the size limit.
